_note: SAMPLE. Generated from the hypothesised draft so the pages can be built and reviewed before Thursday. Replaced by live data on draft day.

roast.text: Keshia took the guy who's finished top two among quarterbacks six years running, in the format where you start two of them. Correct on every axis. I assume she was aiming at something else and hit this by mistake.
Jay watched a running back run start, waited his turn, and took the back who led the league in carries and touchdowns. No risk, no thought, no fingerprints. Somebody hand him a participation lanyard.

Justin took the only player in history with 90 catches in each of his first five seasons. Third among receivers three years straight, and Justin found him with all the effort of a guy grabbing the top magazine at a dentist's office.

Mike spent pick eleven on a quarterback whose rushing production cratered to 421 yards and his worst points per game as a starter. James Cook was right there. Mike paid first-round money for a guy who already downgraded himself.
Evan got handed the league's leading rusher at pick twelve and took him. Nobody's arguing. It's just that when the board does your job, you don't get to call it a strategy.

For Olave at twenty to look smart, the career year has to be the new floor, the nine touchdowns have to repeat, and Breece Hall and Ashton Jeanty both have to fall apart in public. Bree needs three miracles and a funeral.

Etienne's a fine player who changed teams and keeps clearing 1,399 yards. Jesse just paid a second-round price for him while Ashton Jeanty sat there untouched. That's buying the display model at full retail.

Chenell took a receiver who's never played a full 17-game season, which is a strange thing to lean on right after Jayden Higgins tore his ACL. Houston's target share is now one hamstring from being a group text.

Third round, Mahomes, questionable, torn ACL in Week 15. Evan saw a quarterback run break out and joined it holding the one with the medical file. Following the crowd is easier when you don't check what you picked up.

Count Mike's roster. Four quarterbacks, zero running backs, zero receivers, five bench spots to house a position group that can only field two on Sunday. He's drafting a quarterback competition nobody will televise.

McMillan makes the leap, Carolina's offense stops being Carolina's offense, and the one top-10 week from last year turns into eight. Colin's holding Offensive Rookie of the Year and hoping the second act is written by somebody else.

Goff's cleared 4,500 yards and 30 touchdowns three years running, and Keshia grabbed him at fifty-one with nobody better on the board. That's two correct picks in a row. Somebody check whether she's still the one clicking.

Jordan Love was sitting there in the format that starts two quarterbacks, and Tyler took a receiver whose target share fell to sixteen percent. That's paying a premium for a guy Chicago was already done using.

Justin's got Cleveland's tight end and a Cleveland-adjacent theme going. George Pickens was available, but Justin wanted the guy who spent his rookie year outproducing a quarterback merry-go-round, and now he owns a piece of it.

For Pollard to work, Tennessee's offense has to stop being Tennessee's offense, five touchdowns has to become twelve, Tyjae Spears has to vanish, and Zay Flowers has to be a bust. Colin needs all four by Thursday.
Darnold finished 27th among quarterbacks in points per game and went 68th here. Bree passed George Kittle for nine weeks outside the top twenty. Nobody in Seattle would have taken him this early.
Five running backs, two slots, a flex, and one quarterback in a format that starts two. Doug can field a backfield committee and half a passing game, and the meeting is going great.
Sam LaPorta was right there. Chenell spent a seventh-rounder on a receiver coming off a career-low 850 yards, and she still hasn't drafted a single quarterback in the league that starts two of them.
Five receivers, two spots, one flex. Tyler's building a wideout room deep enough that three of them will spend Sunday watching him not have a running back.

Burden has two career top-20 games and a groin injury from August 8th in a red-zone rep. James took him at eighty-one over Rome Odunze, drafting the breakout everybody's been promising since the guy was in college.

For Higgins to pay off, Ja'Marr Chase has to stop existing near the goal line, the seven missed games have to stay in the past, and Mike has to find a running back. He has five quarterbacks and one receiver.
Best player left, real value, nobody's mad. Eight rounds in, though, Evan still has one quarterback in a format that starts two, and Mahomes is the one with the knee.

Henderson had three enormous games and fourteen at 8.3 points, which is a rookie year and a rumor in the same body. James took the guy who owned 25.1 percent of a backfield and called it a running back.

Andrews was top five in points per game for five straight seasons and finished 24th last year, so Colin bought the good version at the sad version's price. Best pick he's made, and he already had a tight end. Nobody teach him what happened.
Dowdle's fine. Bree now has three tight ends for one slot, one quarterback for two, and a backfield of exactly him. She keeps solving problems she doesn't have.

Chenell just drafted the other half of Pittsburgh's backfield split. Warren and Dowdle can now share carries on two different rosters, and she's still sitting on zero quarterbacks in a league that starts two. Four running backs, no passer, and a Steelers replica jersey rack.

Monangai averaged 6.9 touches a game and put up 7.7 points whenever Swift dressed. Bree's holding the one 198-yard afternoon like it's a season ticket. Also the tight end pile is at three now, which is two more than Sunday accepts.

Isaiah Likely was sitting there. Jay took the fourth overall pick who's finished 41st and 39th among receivers, because two years of being serviceable feels like a prospect if you squint. That's five bench spots and a bet on the Ohio State highlight tape.

Wilson's big stretch happened with Jacoby Brissett throwing and Marvin Harrison hurt, and James took him twenty-six players early. Meanwhile he's got one quarterback in the format that starts two. He keeps drafting guys who broke out under conditions he can't reproduce.

Josh Jacobs was there. Jay took the Chiefs receiver who got hurt on his third snap and scored once all year, and he's now got five wideouts for two spots and a flex. That's a merch table with one quarterback behind it.

Aaron Jones finished dead last among 65 backs in forced missed tackle rate and Bree still got value at 116, which is the kind of thing that happens by accident. She now owns an actual second running back. Don't clap, you'll spook her.

So Chenell owns Pittsburgh's running back and now Pittsburgh's new receiver, and Josh Jacobs walked past her again. Five straight 800-yard seasons and 25 touchdowns in 95 games, which is a lot of catching for a guy who never finishes the drive. Still no quarterback.
Josh Jacobs was sitting there and Doug took a receiver he needed six rounds ago. Two wideouts, six running backs, and a committee meeting that's now overran into a second building.

Three quarterbacks, five running backs, two receivers. Jesse has built the front half of a team twice and the back half never showed up. Jacobs is the best player left, which somehow makes the shape worse.
White signed in Washington, so Doug paired him with Diggs and built a Commanders gift shop. Seven running backs for two slots and a flex. The committee has subcommittees now.

Gainwell was the best player left, so credit there. Chenell now has five running backs, four receivers, one tight end and zero quarterbacks in a league that starts two of them. Eleven rounds of avoiding the only position she is contractually required to own.

Croskey-Merritt went eleven picks past his national ADP and Bree grabbed him during a run at the position she actually needs. That's twice tonight she's done the right thing. Somebody is coaching her from off-camera and I want them found.
Engram finished 15th or worse among tight ends in everything that counts, and Jay took him forty picks before anyone in Denver would have. Second tight end, one slot, still one quarterback.

Lloyd has played one game since 2024 and his path to touches is Josh Jacobs facing a potential suspension. James also owns Green Bay's other back. He's now got both halves of a backfield that depends on a hearing.

Thomas averaged 9.9 points a game with Trevor Lawrence throwing, and Justin already owns a piece of Jacksonville's passing game. So he bought the wild card to protect the investment. Five receivers, two slots, and a flex that's already full.

Addison's targets, catches, yards and touchdowns have gone down two years running, so James bought the third draft of a good rookie season. Six receivers, two slots, one quarterback. He's stockpiling the position he can't start more of.
Jeudy caught 48 percent of what came his way and Colin took him thirty-one picks before Cleveland would have. Third tight end already on the bench, one slot to play them in. Nobody else was bidding.

Robinson catches ninety balls a year and almost never near the end zone, which is a fine problem to have if you own a running back. Tyler owns one. Six receivers, three tight ends, and a backfield you could fit in a glovebox.

Ridley missed ten games and caught seventeen passes, and Jay bought that at a premium. Sixth receiver, two slots, still one quarterback in the format that starts two. He's collecting Tennessee memorabilia now.

Shakir is Josh Allen's safety valve, and Keshia already owns Josh Allen. She's now got five quarterbacks and two receivers, one of whom exists mainly to catch passes from another guy on her bench. Buffalo's offense in a jar.

Nailor has never reached thirty catches in a season and now has to beat out three guys in Las Vegas. Doug took him twenty-eight picks early. Seventh running back on the roster and he spent this one on a tryout.

Gadsden had two enormous weeks and then 6.2 points a game for the rest of the year, and Chris Godwin was sitting there. That's a second tight end for one slot from a man who still hasn't found a second quarterback. James collects October.

Samuel's been solid and unspectacular for five straight years, which is honestly the calmest thing Evan's done tonight. Five receivers, three tight ends, three backs. He's assembled a roster that starts strong at the two positions where you can only play one.
Evan took the first defense of the draft in round fourteen, seven hundred and ninety players early, with RJ Harvey on the board. Nobody was coming for Denver. Nobody has ever been coming for Denver.
James took a defense in the fourteenth round with one quarterback on a roster that starts two. The Seahawks won't be covering the OP slot for him. Nothing will, now.
RJ Harvey was there, and Colin took the Rams defense to sit behind four tight ends he can only play one of. The bench is now a tight end waiting room with a security guard.
Jay took Lions D/ST at 163 with 794 better players available, including RJ Harvey.

The off-camera coach is gone. Bree took a defense with RJ Harvey sitting there, a fourth tight end already stacked up for one slot, and one quarterback in a format that starts two, and Philly won't be playing the OP spot for her.

Jesse already owns a pile of running backs, and now he's added the Chargers defense to a roster that's basically a Los Angeles group tour. Six backs, three slots, and a defense he'll root for out of pure geography.

For Aubrey at 169 to be worth it, Dallas has to stall inside the forty every week, the six running backs have to sort themselves into two useful ones, and the tight end has to become three tight ends. Kickers don't fix shape.

RJ Harvey, a running back, was available, and Doug already has seven of those, so instead he took a kicker listed as questionable. The committee finally hired someone from outside and he's calling in sick.

Myers works out if Seattle drives to the twenty-eight and stops there all season, and if two tight ends learn to share one slot, and if five running backs collapse neatly into three. Reigning champ, still counting on geometry.
Fourteen rounds to build a tight end museum and one round to hire the guy who kicks. Bree's OP slot is a folding chair with a name tag on it.
San Francisco's kicker over RJ Harvey, from a manager with three backs and six receivers. Jay spent his last pick on the one position that can't accidentally solve the quarterback problem.
Bates is a fine kicker and James now owns Detroit's defense and Detroit's foot. Still one quarterback. The OP slot goes into the season unstaffed and he filled it with kickoffs.
